appraisal_events.evidence: elle se détourna, et d'un air indifférent et dédaigneux... que je ne pouvais interpréter... que comme une preuve d'outrageant mépris; et sa main esquissait en même temps un geste indécent
appraisal_events.explanation: Gilberte appears to look past the narrator's family as ridiculous and to direct a fixed, dismissive stare and ambiguous gesture at the narrator, which he reads as contemptuous; the narration flags that this reading passes through his own limited childhood understanding, so the exact charge of the act is left uncertain even as its locally wounding effect on him is clear.

appraisal_events.evidence: Ce pauvre Swann, quel rôle ils lui font jouer: on le fait partir pour qu'elle reste seule avec son Charlus, car c'est lui, je l'ai reconnu! Et cette petite, mêlée à toute cette infamie!
appraisal_events.explanation: The grandfather pities Swann as a man maneuvered into absence so his wife can remain alone with Charlus, casting Swann as passive and diminished while implicating Odette in suspected impropriety.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator experiences Gilberte's apparent disdain as painful humiliation, weakening his emotional footing even as it kindles his desire.
The passage explicitly marks him as excluded from the privileged, unknown world her name evokes, a world he will not enter.
The grandfather's pitying remark frames Swann as a man made to play a demeaning, powerless role in his own household.
The grandfather's suspicion that she contrives to be alone with Charlus casts her local standing under a shadow of impropriety.

ambiguities: Gilberte's fixed stare and hand gesture toward the narrator are explicitly filtered through his own admittedly limited childhood 'dictionary of manners'; the text signals his reading of it as insolent contempt may not be reliable, so the exact valence of her act toward him is treated cautiously.

Odette is never named directly in this passage and is identified only via 'la mère de Gilberte' and 'une dame en blanc'; the resolution to Odette relies on contextual inference (Gilberte's parentage) rather than an explicit name in this passage.
